 Determine the First Imminent Threat: 
Bosses are an Imminent Threat to the Hamlet and 
also affect the Dungeon itself. Each Boss has 3 
Levels of Threats. At the beginning of the game, the 
Boss you draw will be at Level 1.
For each boss, there are three types of cards (one of 
each per level):
•	The Boss Description card, which is used to draw 
the threat at the beginning of an act and provides 
flavor text.
•	The Boss Abilities card, with a Combat Abilities 
side and a Threat Abilities side, itself having a 
Dungeon side and a Village side.
•	The Boss Combat card, which will be placed on 
the Monster Posture track and describes the

Until you complete your first couple of Quests and 
are able to face the Boss itself, its passive abilities 
will affect your time in the Dungeon and the Hamlet. 
Find the four Level 1 Ruins Boss Description Card

 Choose Heroes

Take your Level 1 Hero Card and place it next to 
your dashboard. Find your roster of seven Level 1

Dashboard Skill Slots. Leave the rest on the side. 
Your Level 2 and 3 Hero and Skill Cards won’t be 
used until you train to Level them up, so leave them 
in the box for now.
If you find it difficult to choose which Skills you want, 
feel free to use one of our pre-set builds found in 
page 42 of this rulebook.

Bosses are your Imminent Threat. 
Powerful entities that are a 
constant threat to the Hamlet and 
must be dealt with before you can 
enter the Darkest Dungeon.
Each Boss has three versions 
according to the Campaign Level. 
Bosses have two passive threat 
abilities; one for the Hamlet and 
the other for inside the Dungeons. 
They vary from Level to Level.
In order to face a Boss, the Heroes must complete 
two Quests beforehand. When they do so, the 
Boss location is revealed and they can venture off 
to slay it. There is a general Quest Card for every 
Boss, named Face the Threat; when you must face 
one, consult that card for the Dungeon layout and 
Firewood supplies.
Boss Quest
The Threat has shown itself. 
Now is the time to strike! Find 
its lair and eradicate it.
SPECIAL RULES
Set up this Dungeon according 
to the Boss Quest rules. You 
can’t return to the Hamlet 
before you defeat the Boss!

Bosses always hide at the far end of the Dungeon. 
When you are about to set up a Boss Quest 
Dungeon, note how many Rooms the Dungeon Tile 
has on the edge. An Edge Room is a Room that has 
only one Corridor leading to and from it. Take the 
Objective Room along with as many random Room 
Tokens as you need, shuffle them together and 
place them on these Edge Rooms. Then fill up the 
rest of the Room slots as usual. The Boss always 
waits at the edge of the Dungeon. Which edge is 
for you to find out!
 Fighting a Boss 
There is no turning back once you’ve started a 
Face the Threat Quest. You don’t have the option 
to leave the Dungeon and if you fail to defeat the 
Boss, the Campaign is over!
When you enter the Objective Room, use 
the Room Tile that is unique to the Boss 
you are fighting. Each Boss has its own 
Room Tile. 
Flip the Boss Abilities card from the Threat Abilities 
side to the Battle abilities side. The Threats cease 
to function at that moment. As Bosses have special 
Battle rules, take a moment to read them both on 
their card and, for a more extensive explanation, in 
the Boss’ special rules section of this book (page 38) 
in any case, find the Boss Combat card to place it on 
the Monster Posture track.
Do not count Battle Rounds while fighting the Boss. 
When you defeat it, the Battle ends immediately. 
Remove any other Monsters from play – you don’t 
need to fight them.
To form the Initiative Deck, check how many 
actions/round the Boss has and add that many 
Monster Initiative Cards for it in the deck. Do the 
same for any other special Monsters that might 
start the battle along with the Boss. 
When you kill a Boss, the Campaign advances a Level 
and you enter the next Act. 
 Boss Turns 
Since most Bosses have more than one action/
round, they get to act more frequently than other 
Monsters. When Monsters with multiple actions/
round are in Battle, they’ll use the Initiative Cards 
to act before Monsters that are behind them in 
Stance order.
Example: The Shuffling Horror has two actions/
round. The players draw an Initiative Card showing 
it’s the Monsters' turn to go. The Shuffling Horror 
acts and finishes its action.

The old mill hangs listless, suspended in the time-twisting curse of the comet’s impact. The barren fields are awash in 
alien hues, where the shattered husks of the Miller and his farmhands reap a new and terrible harvest…
The Color of Madness Expansion adds a new cooperative stand-alone game mode in which you must survive multiple waves of assaulting enemies 
in the new Farmstead environment. This game mode is not part of the main campaign, and can be played in one 90-minute session. 
This expansion adds 3 new room tiles and associated cards, and delivers 26 new monster miniatures - including 
3 new bosses. A copy of Darkest Dungeon the Board Game is required to play this expansion.

Blight had struck the harvest again that year, and the Miller was desperate. He came to me, 
hat clutched tightly in filthy fingers, stinking of sweat and manure. Seated comfortably in my 
observatory, surrounded by telescopes and other delicate apparatus, I recognized his misfortune 
as an opportunity, and I agreed to lend him my... expertise.
Granite slabs etched with certain celestial designs were erected around the perimeter of the 
Farmstead. The Miller, lamentably eager for some early sign of improvement, fixed his watery 
eyes intently upon the wilted fields and listless mill. My gaze, however, was cast skyward and I 
marveled at the limitless profanity of the stars, wondering what harvest might come.
The poor Miller - thrice a victim. The seasons took his livelihood, I took his land, and now, 
uncountable years later, the comet has taken his humanity. My only regret is that I did not live to 
see that shoddy mill smashed to pieces by the miraculous bounty I reaped from beyond the void.

The Color of Madness is a different kind of expansion for Darkest Dungeon the Board Game. You do not 
use it to expand the core game with new Quests and Monsters, but you will rather play a standalone 
session lasting 90-120 minutes. It uses the core rulebook and some of the core box components, so the 
core game is still needed to play this expansion.
In The Color of Madness, players take on the role of a party of adventurers tasked with investigating 
a nearby farmstead. A strange meteorite landed there, scattering mysterious shards all across the 
area and mutating the fauna. While the other Heroes are fighting off imminent threats and trying to 
clear the way to the Darkest Dungeon, this group of adventurers will try to brave the horrors of the 
farmstead and defeat its Boss to end the threat once and for all.  
As most of the core game rules remain the same, this rulebook will assume you’re already familiar with 
those and will explain only the differences.

Game Setup
1  Place the game board in the middle of the table 
and choose which side you’re playing on.
2 Players choose their Heroes. You must make a 
party of four and all Heroes start at Level 1. Take 
the 8 Initiative Cards (4 Heroes and 4 Monsters) and 
shuffle them together to form the Initiative Deck.
3 Take the Quirks, Afflictions, Virtues and Disease 
Decks of the core game, shuffle them and place 
them to the side of the board. Take the Curio 
Cards and Trinkets from The Color of Madness, 
shuffle them and place them to the side as well.
4  Place all Provisions Dice and conditions and 
Wounds within reach.  
5  Place the Shards, Healing Crystals and Curio 
Tokens within reach.
6  Place the special Light Tracker close to the 
board with the Light Token/miniature on the 
Farmstead Miasma spot.
7  Place the Sleeper’s Dream Monster Card near 
the board. 
8 Construct the Monsters Deck: Separate the 
Level 1 from the Level 2 Monsters and form 
two decks. Take three cards at random from 
each deck and form a third one. Take the three 
special Curio Spawn Cards and shuffle one into 
each deck. Now place the deck with the Level 2 
Monsters on the bottom, place on top of it the 
deck with the mixed Monsters and on top of that 
the deck with the Level 1 Monsters. You should 
have a single Monster Deck now.
9 Pick a Boss at random that you’ll fight at the end. 
Take all its necessary components and place 
them within reach.
10 Have the Special Campsite tile near the board. You’ll 
use it only once, just before you face the Boss.
11 Place the Hero miniatures on the Area indicated 
as 
. Roll four ten-sided dice and place one 
Curio Token on the Areas matching the rolls 
(the number icons). There can be multiple Curio 
Tokens in a single Area. Roll a ten-sided die and 
place the Sleeper’s Dream miniature on the 
corresponding Area.
12 Roll 8 Provisions dice and form your Provisions 
pool.
You are ready to start playing!
Game Overview
In The Color of Madness, the Heroes must survive 
an onslaught of constantly spawning Monsters long 
enough to clear the Area and proceed to fight the 
Boss. The game has three phases: the Onslaught 
phase, the Resting phase and the Boss Fight phase.
Note that the boss does not have any threat ability 
that applies during the first two phases, only a 
combat ability that applies during the final phase  
The game ends in defeat if a Hero dies.
The game ends in victory if the Heroes defeat 
the Boss.
The game starts with the Onslaught phase. 
During this phase, the Heroes will battle wave 
after wave of Monsters. The phase ends when 
either all Monsters have been defeated or when 
the Sleeper’s Dream is killed. End the phase 
immediately after one of the above occurs. 
Once this phase is over, Heroes will proceed to the 
Resting phase. During this phase, they’ll use the 
Campsite Tile to decide how they’ll spend their 
brief moments of calmness before going to fight 
the Boss. Once they rest, they proceed to the final 
phase, the Boss Fight phase. Here they’ll fight a 
Boss in its unique Room with its unique rules, just 
like a Boss fight in the core game.  
 The Light 
The Light works differently in The Color of Madness. 
Instead of moving in a linear fashion, when it 
goes up, the active Hero chooses where to place 
the token, among the following Spots: Blazing, 
Haunting, Splendorous and Gleaming. Once it’s 
done, the written effect takes place immediately 
and it affects all Heroes. The token then stays there. 
A Hero can choose to place the token on the same 
spot when the Light goes up again, still triggering 
the effect. So, if the Light was on the Blazing spot 
and a Hero used a Torch provision, they can choose 
to place it on the same spot again and give the Buff 
 2t to the party.
When the Light drops by any effect, it always returns 
to the Farmstead Miasma spot, making Heroes 
suffer 2 Stress. If the Light is in the Farmstead 
Miasma and drops again, it remains there, but its 
effect still triggers as normal.

Battle! 
Start taking turns using the Initiative Deck as normal.
Monster Turns: Monsters take turns exactly as in 
the core game. 
If a Monster starts or moves in an Area containing 
Healing Crystals (dropped by the Sleeper’s Dream) 
and it is wounded, it immediately consumes them 
(remove the Crystal from play) and 1 for each.
Hero Turns: At the start of their turn, before they 
do anything else, a Hero can choose to Level Up. 
They do so by spending 2 Shards to Level Up a skill 
or 3 Shards to Level Up the Hero. After that, they 
can play their turn as normal. They can take only one 
of these options (no multiple Level Ups).
Turns play in the exact same way as in the core 
game (remove tokens from condition stacks, then 
take actions) with the exception that Heroes have 3 
actions in their turn during this phase. 
Curio Tokens can be interacted with by spending an 
action. When a Hero interacts with a Curio, remove 
it from the board and draw a Curio Card, following 
its instructions as normal.
If a Hero starts or moves into an Area with Healing 
Crystals, they can choose to consume any of them 
as a free action to either 1 or recover 1 Stress 
 
per token consumed.
As previously mentioned, when a monster is killed, 
the heroes gain two shards, and its Monster card is 
discarded.
Special Areas
Some Areas on the board have special rules.
A Infected Area: Heroes entering this Area suffer 
1 
/Hero Level.
B Blessed Area: : Heroes ending their turn here 
gain 
 2t, 2 /Hero Level and recover 4 Stress 
.
C Teleporters: a Hero can move from one teleporter 
to another by spending one movement 
 point 
and suffering +1 Stress 
.
End : The attack phase ends either when all monsters 
have been defeated and the Monster deck is empty 
or when the Sleeper’s Dream is killed.
 Resting Phase 
Once the Heroes are done with the Onslaught 
phase, they can rest. At the start of this phase, 
Heroes are free to spend any remaining Shards they 
have to Level Up as they see fit. Once this is done, 
bring the Campsite tile in the middle of the table.
Heroes can then choose one slot to use on the 
Campsite tile and gain its benefits. Multiple Heroes 
can occupy the same slot. 
After resting is done, Heroes are ready to face the 
Boss!
The Bosses
Fighting the Boss works exactly as in the core game. 
Follow the Boss instructions to see how each Boss 
plays.
Important: Heroes have 2 actions per round in this 
phase.
 
The Miller: When you face the Miller, 
follow these steps:
1
Find the Miller’s Room and put it 
in play. It’s the room

the Aggressive Stance and his miniature on the 
corresponding Area on the board. Shuffle two 
Initiative Cards for the Miller into the Initiative Deck.
3
Have the Frozen Farmhand miniatures along 
with their cards, ready to the side.
The Master Beckons:  If there are no other Monsters 
in play, The Miller will summon a Frozen Farmhand 
in the Aggressive Stance (moving the Miller in the 
Defensive Stance) and another one in the Support 
Stance. When they turn to Farmhands II, they have 
 at all times (cannot be removed). Make sure you 
replace with a random Farmhand II (as one of them 
will drop the Light) and transfer all Wounds the 
Frozen Farmhand had already suffered. 
Return the initiative card to the deck, and the Frozen 
Farmhand II thus created will be activated this round.
When the Miller is defeated, the fight ends and the 
party is victorious!

Seeds of Despair: When the Focus Point/
Aberrations’ turn comes, roll 3 ten-sided dice 
and place three Focus Point Tokens on the
